title: September DMI gave no clear added rain-difference prediction gain for two tropical regions in 2000-2025
abstract: We tested whether September DMI adds prediction information for the October-December rain difference between East Africa (5 S-5 N, 35-40 E) and the Maritime Continent (10 S-10 N, 95-140 E). Earlier-year fits used both regions' September rain, Nino 3.4 and year. Across 26 tests in 2000-2025, adding DMI reduced mean squared error by 22.79%. The conditional 95% three-year block interval was -0.37% to 39.87%. Thus the added gain remains uncertain. The two-region mean gain was 1.02%. An exact error decomposition assigned 49.34% of the difference-target point reduction to the cross-region error term. This does not establish a physical cause. The difference gain fell to 5.20% with August inputs and 7.40% without a trend. Short records, revised and interim products, release delays, domain choice and conditional uncertainty limit inference. Original code, source hashes, aggregate scores and a figure are included. External records and individual predictions can be regenerated outside the package.
